articles.title: Pharrell gets mistaken as another rapper at World Cup final
Patience beats overreliance on Messi: how the final was won and lost
articles.description: Argentina tried to kill the spectacle and make it a physical battle but Spain refused to take the bait and kept passing A worrying thought as a tepid first half drew to a close: was the half-time show going to be better than the football? This was a slog. Argentina could not match Spain’s possession approach but they had ways to level the playing field. There was physicality from Lionel Scaloni’s side, whose aim was to kill the spectacle before taking control in the second half, and they were allowed to take it to the limit by the Slovenian referee, Slavko Vincic. Alexis Mac Allister could have been booked for an early foul on Dani Olmo and the leniency, together with a pitch not conducive to playing flowing football, allowed Argentina to disrupt Spain’s passing game, creating the conditions for one of the most tedious World Cup finals. articles.title: Trump Goons Turn World Cup Into Make-a-Wish Outing
articles.description: Eva Marie Uzcategui - FIFA / FIFA via Getty Images President Donald Trump’s closest allies are treating the FIFA World Cup like a day at the beach. The 80-year-old president’s family, friends, Cabinet members, and political allies were spotted living it up at the world’s biggest sporting event on Sunday, soaking up the sun and squeezing the most out of their status as Spain and Argentina battled it out on the field for the title of world champions. Trump’s daughter, Ivanka, shared a few stories on Instagram highlighting her attendance at the event, including a video of her father gazing down at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, as Marine One prepared to land.
